edges.description: Loss of functional COA5 impairs early complex IV assembly; patient-cell rescue attributes the defect to COA5.
Loss of COA5/PET191 disrupts COX2 assembly-factor interactions in engineered HEK293T cells. Transfer of this precise intermediate to p.Ala53Pro patient cells remains provisional.

Impaired recruitment of COX2 maturation factors provides a candidate explanation for failure to incorporate mature MTCO2. The exact connection to the patient missense assembly defect remains unresolved.
Impaired formation of mature complex IV reduces cytochrome c oxidase activity. Wild-type COA5 restores complex IV activity in patient fibroblasts.
Failure to assemble mature complex IV limits its incorporation into respiratory supercomplexes in COA5 knockout U2OS cells.
Reduced oxidative metabolism provides a plausible route to increased lactate production. Pyruvate flux and the intervening metabolic steps were not measured in COA5 patients.
Impaired mitochondrial energy production plausibly contributes to myocardial remodeling. The tissue-specific steps from the assembly defect to hypertrophy have not been resolved.
The enzymatic defect is measured as reduced cytochrome c oxidase activity.
edges.target: Decreased Activity of Mitochondrial Complex IV

edges.description: Lactate accumulation accompanies the documented severe lactic acidosis.
Systemic lactate accumulation is accompanied by increased urinary lactate.
The remodeling response is expressed as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
Septal hypertrophy is a component of the hypertrophic remodeling.
Patient fibroblasts accumulate an early COX1-containing intermediate and have reduced mature complex IV. Wild-type COA5 restores complex IV activity.
edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are not an affected tissue in this cardiac-dominant disorder, so nothing about the cardiomyopathy can be read out here. The cells also grow poorly, which the 2025 authors identify as a practical limit on further experimentation.

edges.description: The knockout reproduces the patients' isolated Complex IV defect and resolves it further: MTCO1-containing subcomplexes accumulate, MTCO2 is absent, and the holoenzyme is lost, placing the COA5 step between MTCO1 maturation and MTCO2 incorporation.
edges.limitations: U2OS is a heterologous osteosarcoma line. The engineered c.287_290+3del deletion causes undetectable COA5 protein on complexome profiling, unlike the patient missense genotype. Cardiac remodeling and infantile lethality lie outside this cellular model.
edges.source: CRISPR/Cas9 COA5 knockout U2OS cell line

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts accumulate an early COX1/MTCO1-containing intermediate lacking COX2, COX4 and COX5b, with reduced mature complex IV. In COA5 knockout U2OS cells, complexome profiling places the block between MTCO1 maturation and MTCO2 incorporation. Complete loss of the holocomplex in knockout cells should not be equated with complete loss in patient fibroblasts.
